title: Client Subsidy Terms Printed against Each Micro Market Format
content:
How client money reaches an employee at the kiosk is fixed by the market format. Each format in the Unattended Micro Market Program prints a subsidy model, the share of shelf price met where the model meets a share, the ceiling on subsidy drawn for one employee on one day, the smallest single funding lot the client may pay in, and the months a funding lot stays drawable.

| Market format | Subsidy model | Share of shelf price met, per cent | Daily ceiling for one employee, USD | Smallest funding lot, USD | Months a lot stays drawable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cooler & Snack Wall | no subsidy is met | 0 | 0 | 750 | 6 |
| Compact Micro Market | a share of shelf price | 10 | 3 | 1800 | 9 |
| Standard Micro Market | a share of shelf price | 20 | 5.5 | 4200 | 12 |
| Fresh Food Micro Market | a share of shelf price | 25 | 7.5 | 8500 | 12 |
| Expanded Campus Micro Market | a flat amount once per shopping visit | 0 | 6 | 16000 | 12 |
| Smart Store Micro Market | a share of shelf price | 30 | 9 | 6500 | 12 |

## Boundary readings

A format whose model meets no share of shelf price prints that share as 0. The Cooler & Snack Wall meets nothing at all and prints a daily ceiling of 0 USD; the Expanded Campus Micro Market meets a flat amount once per shopping visit and prints a share of shelf price of 0 against a daily ceiling of 6 USD. The four formats that meet a share of shelf price print 10, 20, 25 and 30 per cent respectively.

The smallest funding lot rises with the format, from 750 USD on the Cooler & Snack Wall to 16000 USD on the Expanded Campus Micro Market, with the Smart Store Micro Market at 6500 USD. A lot stays drawable for 6 months on the Cooler & Snack Wall, 9 months on the Compact Micro Market and 12 months on each of the other four formats.
